newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BA still hopeful of American deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BA still hopeful of American deal.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Tuesday it remained as hopeful as ever that its proposed link-up with American Airlines will be approved by the two governments but admitted the process was taking longer than expected.
"I remain more or less as optimistic as I was at the beginning (when the deal was announced in June)," chief executive Robert Ayling told Reuters in an interview.

BA and American have been waiting for nearly two months for British trade minister Ian Lang to decide whether or not to block the deal ever since his Office of Fair Trading (OFT) completed an investigation into the competition issues.

There has been industry speculation that Lang is still having trouble trying to reconcile the conflicting arguments for and against allowing the alliance to go through without a full investigation by the UK Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

"It is taking longer than we thought partly because the international aviation market is complex and the competition issues which arise from such transactions are not straightforward," Ayling said on Tuesday.
"The competition authorities here in Britain have approachecd it with a great deal of care and not rushed to judgement," he said.
